title: Targeted comparisons against simpler configurations
labels: DETERMINISTIC FIXTURE PROVIDER — scripted workers in real processes; no model was run
SYNTHETIC DATA — every request, team, dataset and value is invented
INJECTED DEFECTS — in about half of the episodes one worker's first attempt carries a defect its own tests do not catch

ASSUMED RATES — how often defects occur, and how often two workstreams disagree about an interface nobody agreed, are parameters of this testbed. The comparisons show what each coordination step catches and costs when those things happen; they do not show how often they happen in real work.

steps.claim: The simpler configuration is a coordination-level candidate with its own version
steps.observed: coordination v1 → candidate: Sets independent_verification to false: no verification swarm is formed and the integrated result is accepted on delivery's own combined tests.

steps.claim: Both configurations run the same seeded missions end to end
steps.observed: 8 complete fixture missions per configuration from held-out set missions-A; a defect is injected into a first attempt in about half of them

steps.claim: The simpler configuration really is cheaper and faster
steps.observed: worker invocations per mission 12.875 → 10; completion 3795 ms → 2825 ms

steps.claim: What it gives up is measured by an oracle, not assumed
steps.observed: defects reaching an accepted result per mission 0 → 0.625; truly correct missions 1 → 0.375 (difference -0.625, 95% interval -0.875 to -0.25)

steps.claim: The decision follows the frozen rule
steps.observed: reject: Rejected: no more defects escape failed. Acceptance criteria that fail on results the mission accepted: candidate 5, incumbent 0, across 8 episodes.

steps.claim: A second simplification is put to the same gate: no interface agreement before parallel work
steps.observed: Removes the interface-agreement step: no contract task, and delivery workstreams take the acceptance criteria as input instead of a pinned contract. Run on missions-B; the workstreams disagreed about the shared record in 5 of 8 episodes (an assumed rate).

steps.claim: The cost of the step and the cost of going without it are both measured
steps.observed: the agreement step costs 1 worker invocations and 258 ms per mission; a mission where the workstreams disagreed cost 1 more invocations and 796.2 ms more than the same mission with the agreement

steps.claim: Integration failures and quality are reported, not assumed
steps.observed: integration failures per mission 0 → 0.625; truly correct missions 1 → 1; invocations 11.75 → 12 (difference 0.25, 95% interval -0.5 to 0.75); completion 3407 ms → 3808 ms

steps.claim: The decision follows the frozen rule, whatever it is
steps.observed: inconclusive: No demonstrated improvement: truly_correct_missions is no worse (95% interval 0 to 0, margin 0), but cost did not fall (worker_invocations_per_mission changed by 0.25), so the simplification saves nothing.
